About this assessment

This is a 5-part skills test completed for Underwave Training, a data-driven advertising agency. The brief covered real-world EA tasks: a client sales deck, a performance tracking report, CEO calendar management, a full project management plan, and professional email handling. All brand data and scenarios are fictional and created for the exercise.

Part 2

Weekly Performance Tracking Report

Brief: Build a weekly ad performance report from raw data. Include calculated metrics (ROAS, CPL, CPP, Conversion Rate), a summary section, and 2–3 data-driven insights. Evaluated on accuracy, formula logic, organization, and quality of analysis.
DateAd SpendRevenueLeadsPurchasesROASCPLCPPConv. Rate

Total / Avg$5,700$13,1006601292.36x$8.59$45.1820.0%
Insight 01

Day 3 was the top performer: highest ROAS (3.11x), lowest CPP ($30), highest conversion rate (27.3%), at the week's lowest spend ($900). Efficiency, not volume, drove the result.

Insight 02

Higher spend ≠ better outcomes. Day 4 had the highest spend ($1,500) but only 2.0x ROAS and $53.57 CPP. Budget should follow performance signals, not volume.

Insight 03

Conversion rate swung from 14.3% to 27.3% across the week. Lead quality varies more than lead volume, making conversion rate optimization the higher-leverage lever for reducing CPP.

Part 3

Calendar Management — CEO Day Schedule

Brief: Schedule a full CEO workday with 7 competing requests across fixed and flexible time windows. Provide a final schedule and a written rationale explaining the prioritization logic.

The 7 requests:
1. Internal team meeting – 30 mins (must happen between 9 AM – 12 PM)
2. Client call (Brand A) – 45 mins (flexible between 10 AM – 3 PM)
3. Podcast recording – 1 hour (fixed at 1 PM)
4. Lunch break – 1 hour (between 12 PM – 2 PM)
5. Candidate interview – 30 mins (before 5 PM)
6. Deep work block – 2 hours (no interruptions)
7. Follow-up calls – 2 calls, 20 mins each

Scheduling Logic

The internal team meeting was scheduled first at 9:00 AM to align priorities at the start of the day. The deep work block was placed immediately after (10:00–12:00) to protect the CEO's peak focus hours, with 30 minutes after the meeting to capture notes and clear the inbox.

Lunch at 12:00 flows directly into the fixed podcast recording at 1:00 PM, keeping the transition seamless. The afternoon was reserved for all external interactions: client call, follow-up calls with a 10-minute buffer between each, and the candidate interview, batched together to minimize context switching. The day wraps up just before 5 PM.

Part 4

Project Management Plan — 14-Day Campaign Launch

Brief: Build a 14-day project plan for a DTC brand campaign launch: 15 video ads, 3 creators, media buying setup, landing page updates, and weekly reporting. Must include task breakdown, timeline, ownership, status tracking, dependencies, and risks. Built in Asana.

Brief approval → All production

Client must approve the creative brief by May 6 before any creator shoots or production work can begin. Most critical dependency in the project.

Creator shoots → Content review

All 3 creators must submit footage before the content review (May 10), which must be complete before final video editing starts (May 14).

Pixel setup → Media buying

Conversion tracking must be verified before campaigns are configured. Running ads without confirmed tracking means no reliable performance data.

Client approval + landing page → QA

Both final ad approval and the live landing page must be complete before the QA check on May 16, which must pass before launch on May 17.
